title: Interview set-up; interviewee's personal data
description: The interviewer explains confidentiality and the release form, then gathers Myra Jeanne Stark's personal details. She records her maiden name Anderson, her birth in Coeur d'Alene, Idaho, in 1940, and her nickname Fifth.

title: Mother's background; father's background and businesses
description: Stark gives details about her mother Vivian Hastings, born in Palouse, Washington, a housewife who helped in the family businesses. She then describes her father Myron William Anderson, born in Colorado, a mechanic, welder and sawmill worker who owned garages, worked on outboard motors and built aluminum boats.

title: Siblings; husband Martin and his mining work; children
description: Stark identifies her brother Irving and her husband Martin H. Stark, whom she married in North Carolina in November 1973. She explains that he is a contract miner for Bunker Hill paid per amount of ore, and names her three children, Marian, Michael Shane and Jack Raymond Isbell, all born in Coeur d'Alene.

title: Schooling and jobs; selling Tupperware
description: Stark lists her education at Coeur d'Alene high school and beauty school, and her jobs engraving lenses at Clark Pindar, at the Post Falls Cannery and at a self-serve station. She explains that she sells Tupperware in Kellogg for sociability and flexibility, since she considers homemaking her full-time job.

title: Hobbies; hunting and shooting; clubs
description: Stark lists motorcycles, sports and knitting as her interests, and describes elk, deer and grouse hunting with her husband and parents. She learned to shoot through the school NRA rifle club, earning medals, though she no longer belongs to a rifle club.

title: Life outline; three marriages and divorces
description: Stark outlines her life, limited travel, and her three marriages: a first marriage arranged because of pregnancy, a second that failed after her husband became an alcoholic and beat her and the children, and her remarriage to Martin. Her daughter Marianne, present, recalls being beaten and feeling happy about the divorce, and Stark says the boys have largely accepted Martin as their father.

title: Meeting Martin; muzzle-loader hunting; recreation; mining safety
description: Stark describes meeting Martin at a Kellogg bar after her divorce, their courtship, and their shared hunting, including a muzzle-loader hunt near St. Mary's and casting their own bullets. She covers motorcycle trips, childhood swimming and water skiing on Coeur d'Alene Lake, her lens-engraving job ended by allergies, cannery work, natural childbirth, college hopes for her children, and her unconcern about Martin's underground mining work for Bunker Hill.

title: Husband's mining work; pollution; wartime; teen pregnancy; decision-making; canning; hobbies; mechanical skills; women's work; parenting; prostitution
description: Myra Jeanne Stark discusses her husband's mining work and his enjoyment of underground jobs, then addresses pollution and lead in Kellogg. She shares her father's World War II service, brother's Navy career, and teenage pregnancy experience. The conversation covers family decision-making, her canning and hobbies, mechanical abilities, independent views on women's work in mining, working mothers, family outings, and driving lessons. It concludes with a discussion on prostitution's community impact and family dynamics.

title: Marriage and career; sibling relationships; peer pressure; moving and community
description: A young woman discusses her desire for marriage and family over career, challenges of living in the house, preference for outdoor activities, and planning for two children. She describes sibling dynamics with her brothers, occasional resistance to peer drinking and smoking, and her close friendship. She also reflects on moving from Korea to Coeur d'Alene, gaining more friends and experiencing less bullying.
